detail: CONFIRMED by execution at HEAD d649ec4 (workflow wf_daceaa5d-eee lane V2, scratch vitest in an isolated worktree): readRecord() returns null for an unparseable file (record-ingest.ts:81-91), the loop `continue`s at :243-245 BEFORE fileIds.add, and the deletion pass at :291-296 removes the db row → stats {deleted:1, skipped:1}; the embedding is swept as an orphan by the next reconcile (embedding-reconcile.ts:77-83); after the file is repaired the record re-inserts as a NEW row (seq 1→2, vector regenerated). The `typeof record.id !== 'string'` branch (:244) is fully silent — no warning, no skipped++. A parseable file whose body id ≠ filename stem inserts a stray row under the body id and deletes the stem's row. The existing test 'skips unparseable record files without deleting them' (test/record-sync.test.ts:539-553) never seeds a row, so deleted is trivially 0 and never asserted — a false positive for the docblock guarantee. Field relevance (2026-09-04 report #3/#4): their tier-A merge queue evicts conflicted records/ entries and the next server start ingests the tree unconditionally (backend-factory.ts:130-133), so a marker-laden file deletes that ULID's row on every host that ingests it — presenting as an EMPTY assemble, exactly their host-B symptom class. Fix (planned 2.16.1): before parsing, `if (dbRows.has(stem)) fileIds.add(stem)` for every file; refuse insert/update when body id ≠ stem; count + warn in the non-string-id branch; rewrite the test to seed a row. This is a narrow, recorded exception to DD-8 (an unreadable file is not a file and cannot 'win'); precedence for parseable files is unchanged. Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-05-cross-host-sync-plan.md.
summary: Ingest DELETES the sqlite row for any record file it cannot parse or identify (conflict markers, 0-byte, non-string id, id≠stem) while the file stays on disk — docblock :19 promises the opposite
